scenicChapters.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline
scenicChapters.narrative: For 44 km this is Bandai-Azuma Skyline, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 17.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Bandai-Azuma Skyline
scenicChapters.narrative: 1240 m come off over 40 km at around 5.5%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

bandai-azuma-skyline.story: 96 km one way from Fukushima - plan on about 1 h 39 of riding. It goes by way of Jododaira and Tsuchiyu Pass. The highest point is about 1,250 m. Tsuchiyu Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It suits an unhurried touring pace.

scenicChapters.title: Parco Pluritematico → Fiavé-Lago Carera
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 55 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
